interest: This file provides valuable insight into the intersection of international private law, banking regulation, and diplomatic relations during the Great Depression. It illustrates how the sharp devaluation of the Japanese yen in 1931–1932 directly impacted Japanese immigrant depositors in the United States, creating disputes over foreign exchange liabilities and the legal responsibilities of foreign bank agencies operating in New York. Additionally, the file highlights the strict jurisdictional boundaries observed by the U.S. State Department, demonstrating its reliance on Article VII of the 1911 Treaty of Commerce and Navigation and state banking statutes to disclaim regulatory authority over private banking controversies despite mounting political tensions between Japan and the United States.
keywords: Treaty of Commerce and Navigation of 1911
overview: This file (894.51611/1–2) centers on an inquiry submitted to Secretary of State Henry L. Stimson by Philadelphia attorney Daniel R. Rothermel concerning the legal status and operations of the Yokohama Specie Bank, Ltd. in New York. Rothermel represented the court-appointed guardian of Shoraku Maki (alias Samuel Mack), an incapacitated Japanese national institutionalized in Philadelphia, who held yen certificates of deposit that the bank's New York agency refused to redeem in dollars at pre-depreciation exchange rates, eventually insisting that payment could only be made in Japan. The file includes Rothermel's detailed petition and follow-up inquiry, an internal Department of State Legal Adviser memorandum prepared for Eugene H. Dooman advising on jurisdictional limitations, and the official departmental reply signed by Stanley K. Hornbeck disclaiming federal regulatory authority over banking, referring the complainant to New York State banking authorities, and citing Article VII of the 1911 Treaty of Commerce and Navigation with Japan.

subfiles.about: Inquiry from an attorney requesting State Department intervention regarding the refusal of the Yokohama Specie Bank in New York to honor certificates of deposit held by an incapacitated Japanese national.
subfiles.summary: Daniel R. Rothermel, attorney for the guardian of Shoraku Maki (alias Samuel Mack), an incompetent Japanese national confined in the Philadelphia Hospital for Mental Diseases, petitions Secretary of State Henry L. Stimson regarding ¥4,407.93 in certificates of deposit issued by the Yokohama Specie Bank. Rothermel outlines the bank's successive refusals to redeem the certificates in dollars at pre-1932 exchange rates, noting that the bank first cited New York banking restrictions against deposit accounts, then offered a drastically reduced sum following the yen's depreciation, and finally demanded presentation of the certificates in Japan. He requests advice on the bank's legal status in the United States and urges the State Department to investigate foreign banking activities.
subfiles.title: Letter from Daniel R. Rothermel to Secretary of State Henry L. Stimson regarding deposits of Shoraku Maki in the Yokohama Specie Bank

subfiles.about: Department of State reply informing Rothermel that the federal government lacks regulatory authority over banking institutions and citing the 1911 commercial treaty with Japan.
subfiles.from: Stanley K. Hornbeck (for the Secretary of State)
keywords: Treaty of Commerce and Navigation of 1911
subfiles.summary: Writing on behalf of the Secretary of State, Far Eastern Affairs Division Chief Stanley K. Hornbeck acknowledges Daniel R. Rothermel's letter of November 21, 1932, regarding the deposit dispute with the Yokohama Specie Bank. Hornbeck explains that the Department of State possesses no jurisdiction over banking institutions and advises Rothermel to address his complaints to the New York State banking authorities. He further quotes Article VII of the 1911 Treaty of Commerce and Navigation between the United States and Japan, noting that while foreign commercial and financial companies may appear in American courts, their permission to conduct business remains entirely subject to domestic and local laws.
subfiles.title: Letter from Stanley K. Hornbeck to Daniel R. Rothermel regarding the legal status and regulation of Japanese branch banks

subfiles.about: Internal memorandum from the Legal Adviser recommending specific additions and treaty citations for the Department's draft reply to Daniel R. Rothermel.
keywords: Treaty of Commerce and Navigation of 1911
subfiles.summary: The Office of the Legal Adviser submits proposed drafting changes to Eugene H. Dooman of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs concerning the reply to Daniel R. Rothermel. The memorandum recommends incorporating explicit summaries of the Yokohama Specie Bank's refusal to pay and Rothermel's demand for a departmental investigation. It also supplies standard boilerplate disclaiming federal supervisory jurisdiction over banking corporations, refers the matter to New York State banking law, and provides the full text of Article VII of the 1911 Treaty of Commerce and Navigation with Japan.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from the Legal Adviser to Eugene H. Dooman (Division of Far Eastern Affairs) regarding draft reply to Daniel R. Rothermel

subfiles.about: Follow-up inquiry asking whether the State Department received Rothermel's November 21 letter and when a response may be expected.
subfiles.summary: Daniel R. Rothermel writes a brief follow-up inquiry to Secretary of State Henry L. Stimson regarding the case of Shoraku Maki. Rothermel inquires whether his letter of November 21, 1932, was received by the Department and when he might anticipate receiving an official reply. The document bears Department of State receipt stamps indicating receipt by the Division of Far Eastern Affairs on December 2, 1932.
subfiles.title: Letter from Daniel R. Rothermel to Secretary of State Henry L. Stimson inquiring about status of earlier correspondence
